drhp.business: Pfizer Limited operates in one business segment, Pharmaceuticals, covering manufacturing, marketing, distribution, trading and export of pharmaceutical products, which accounted for 94.34% of turnover in FY 2025-26. The Company sells across 15 therapy areas with a portfolio of over ~125 SKUs organised into Vaccines, Internal Medicine (cardiovascular care, neuroscience, women's health, gastroenterology, pain management and nutrition), Hospitals/anti-infectives and Inflammation & Immunology. risks.note: BRSR names this a Risk & Opportunity: failure to maintain product quality and safety may adversely impact patient wellbeing and the Company's reputation and may expose it to litigation or penalty, with the stated negative financial implications being reputational damage, financial liability, product recalls and shortages. Mitigation rests on the Quality Management System, employee training and the grievance redressal mechanism.

Market growth may be moderated by the regulated pricing environment under the Drug (Price Control) Order; price was the predominant IPM growth driver (4.4% of 9.9%), so pricing restraint bears directly on realisation. Management separately lists pricing controls among its key risks.
risks.risk: Regulated pricing environment and price controls

risks.note: IPM growth may be moderated by the increasing share of trade and non-branded generics; trade generics were around 12% of the market by value in 2025 and are expanding from acute into chronic therapies, implying a market-share shift away from branded generics and moderation of overall market growth.
risks.risk: Competition from trade generics and non-branded generics

risks.note: CDSCO reforms, GMP enforcement, strengthened pharmacovigilance, the proposed Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics Act 2025, evolving impurity-profiling and testing expectations, and the revised UCPMP marketing code raise compliance costs and operational complexity, and may require additional investment in quality systems and supply chain readiness.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance intensity in pharmaceuticals

risks.note: Management flags continuing geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions as factors that may impact business performance; the sourcing chain runs through fellow subsidiaries abroad (for example purchases of stock-in-trade and raw/bulk materials from Pfizer Service Company BVBA, Belgium).
risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and geopolitical exposure

risks.note: BRSR identifies climate change as a Risk: heightened negative effects on human health, increasing frequency of severe weather events affecting communities, personnel and operations, and potential reduced access to essential medicines and vaccines due to value chain disruptions. Mitigation is anchored in parent Pfizer Inc.'s GHG reduction commitments and onsite solar at the Goa site.

Listed by management among the key risks in the current environment, managed through the structured Enterprise Risk Management framework with continuous monitoring, defined mitigation plans and governance oversight.

The Company operates in one business segment (Pharmaceuticals, 94.34% of turnover) from a single national plant with exports only 3.8% of turnover, so performance is tied to the Indian pharmaceutical market. Reach for several established brands now depends on the exclusive supply and marketing arrangement with Cipla Limited, an arrangement that also drove permanent-employee turnover to 37% in FY 2025-26 from 15% the prior year.
risks.risk: Concentration - single segment, single plant and partner-dependent distribution
